Originally, I only started doing it because medical school, PA school, all higher level medicine type graduate studies really like seeing volunteering in medicine. Over my time though, I've grown to really enjoy it. Since I'm not a tech, or nurse, I can't do many hands-on things, so most of my day is spent cleaning the hospital beds, moving patients to other rooms, answering call lights, and stocking rooms, IV carts, whatnot. But after having been there for almost a year the techs and nurses, even a few doctors have learned my name and work ethic and so will pull me aside, even if I'm cleaning a room and ask if I want to observe a procedure or can help them directly with a patient.

Now I've worked as an EMT before and medical assistant, but not in an ER. The things in there are sometimes really cool, and really fucked up. I've been able to watch things from draining an infected bursa with 1500ccs of fluid, to resetting a broken elbow, to holding down unconscious patients when a doc needs to put a main line in.

If medicine is your thing, and you're interested in seeing what happens in the ERs, go volunteer there!
